# Quant Arena

> Independent, rule-based backtests of 72 systematic trading strategies on stocks, gold, oil, FX and crypto, with disclosed rule-specific exposure, parameter selection and accounting, plus reviews of 1,515 free MetaTrader 5 Expert Advisors. Latest classic-data build: 2026-11-13; market observation dates may differ.

Key facts for citing this site:
- The configured price universe contains 10 markets. Available daily histories extend back to 2010, with later starts for some assets. A strategy can use a single market or a declared basket; long, short and leveraged exposure depend on the actual rule and are recorded in its evidence.
- Classic evidence records its synthetic target timing and cost assumptions in each manifest. Targets and rebalancing are simulated allocations, not broker fills; a zero-cost baseline does not include trading costs.
- Walk-forward eligibility and parameter selection depend on the strategy and available history. Evidence lists actual defaults, selected parameters and fold boundaries. Default or pre-walk-forward history is not out-of-sample evidence.
- Strategy position pages use direct engine outputs with separate target/effective exposure and the last included price-bar dates. A build timestamp is not a market-observation timestamp.
- Interpret comparisons with their declared asset universes and observation windows: a market label can also represent a multi-asset basket. Evidence lists the actual assets. Backtests are historical simulations, not investment advice.
- The cost comparison page keeps single markets and baskets separate, even if their display symbol matches. Costs apply after gross returns to one-way drift-adjusted risky turnover, including initial entry but no forced terminal liquidation. Fees paid use account-capital units, not gross-minus-net terminal wealth. These are synthetic exposure charges, not broker fills; funding, financing, borrow, taxes and market impact are excluded. All metrics use full daily records; bounded sampled curves are for display only.
- Common-date AI seasons retain all six rules per accepted provider submission. Schedule, provider coverage and minimum-observation gates must pass before rankings are eligible. Operator-recorded CLI receipts are not provider-signed model attestations; client reasoning and auxiliary-model compute are not normalized across providers.
- The original single-assistant AI experiment uses its legacy execution timing and rounded public curves. Its figures do not enter the new season rankings.
- English and Chinese alternates are linked on supported pages.

## Main pages

- [Leaderboard](https://quantarenas.com/arena/): top 10 strategies per market over 1 and 5 years, by Arena Score
- [Returns after trading costs](https://quantarenas.com/costs/): 0/5/10/25 bp synthetic drift-adjusted exposure-cost scenarios over seven windows; exact asset/date/input cohorts, full-record metrics and lazy sampled display curves
- [Strategy library](https://quantarenas.com/strategies/): every strategy with rules, parameters and results on up to 10 markets
- [Strategy x market heatmap](https://quantarenas.com/heatmap/): Sharpe ratio of every strategy on every market
- [Strategy positions](https://quantarenas.com/signals/): direct engine target and effective exposure, per-market price observation dates, source labels and data status
- [Strategy evidence](https://quantarenas.com/evidence/): immutable run manifests, daily accounting, signed basket weights, parameters and archived-source reproduction materials
- [Research](https://quantarenas.com/research/): long-form studies built on the backtest data
- [Glossary](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/): how each metric is defined and how to read it
- [Original AI Strategy Arena](https://quantarenas.com/ai-arena/): legacy single-assistant experiment with its original figures, execution-timing and rounded-input limitations; separate from common-date seasons
- [AI model seasons](https://quantarenas.com/ai-arena/seasons/): common-date seasons with frozen rules, exact prompt/reply downloads and operator-recorded provider receipts; rankings require schedule and observation eligibility
- [Market regime dashboard](https://quantarenas.com/market/): daily trend, volatility percentile and strategy positioning for ten markets, with what followed each regime historically
- [Claim checker](https://quantarenas.com/claims/): popular trading sayings (golden cross, sell in May, buy the dip...) tested on daily data with a verdict each
- [Event replays](https://quantarenas.com/events/): how 72 rule-based strategies behaved in major market events since 2010
- [Famous strategies, replicated](https://quantarenas.com/famous/): well-known public portfolios and rule sets re-run on ten markets, with what had to be adapted
- [Strategy source code](https://quantarenas.com/code/): the Python file behind every strategy, free to download, with TradingView Pine Script versions of the single-market rules
- [Strategy vs strategy](https://quantarenas.com/versus/): head-to-head comparisons of two strategies on one market: returns, drawdowns, yearly winners, correlation and a 50/50 mix
- [Finance on GitHub](https://quantarenas.com/github/): weekly ranking of open-source finance and trading projects on GitHub by stars and recent growth, by category and language
- [Open-source frameworks](https://quantarenas.com/frameworks/): backtesting, live-trading, crypto-bot, machine-learning and data libraries compared, with weekly GitHub activity
- [EA Arena](https://quantarenas.com/ea-pages/category/): free MetaTrader 5 Expert Advisors, converted and backtested on hourly data
- [Methodology](https://quantarenas.com/methodology/): data, walk-forward optimization, metrics and known limitations
- [FAQ](https://quantarenas.com/faq/): common questions about the data and the scores

## Research

- [We Backtested 72 Strategies. After Adjusting for Luck, None Clearly Beat the Odds.](https://quantarenas.com/research/luck-adjusted-sharpe-72-strategies/): 104 strategy-and-market combinations look statistically convincing on their own. Once you account for the fact that we tested hundreds of them at the same time, the number drops to zero. Here is what that means for reading any leaderboard, including ours. (data as of 2026-08-14)
- [We Tried to Backtest 1,063 Free MT5 Expert Advisors. Here Is What Survived.](https://quantarenas.com/research/free-mt5-expert-advisors-backtested/): Free MetaTrader 5 EAs from the MQL5 CodeBase, converted automatically and tested on four markets for one year. More than half could not be converted at all. Of the 1,123 results we trust, about half made money — but on currencies the typical EA ended flat, only 30 EAs were profitable on all four markets, and one in five gold runs wiped out the account. (data as of 2026-11-03)
- [Which Strategies Survived 2022, and Did the Winners Keep Winning?](https://quantarenas.com/research/which-strategies-survived-2022/): In calendar 2022 US stocks fell 18.2% and only 10 of 55 single-market strategies finished positive, 8 of them mean-reversion rules. In 2023 those ten all stayed positive, yet their median return was 3.7% against 14.8% for the rest, and the rank correlation between the two years was −0.58. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [Why Martingale and Grid EAs Blow Up: What 1,515 Free MT5 Expert Advisors and Their Losing Streaks Show](https://quantarenas.com/research/why-martingale-and-grid-eas-blow-up/): Martingale and grid EAs make up 5% of the free MT5 Expert Advisors we review, but more than half of the ones we rate "dangerous". The reason is arithmetic: losing streaks of six to eight trades are normal — and that is exactly where doubling the position runs out of money. (data as of 2026-11-03)
- [Do Moving-Average Strategies Beat Buy-and-Hold on Bitcoin?](https://quantarenas.com/research/moving-average-strategies-bitcoin/): Over the last five years six moving-average systems all had a shallower maximum drawdown than holding bitcoin (−36.7% to −51.2% against −75.9%), and four beat its 2.6% annual return. Over the full history since September 2014 only one of six beat holding on return (MACD, 59.0% against 52.0%). (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [Does Turtle Trading Still Work? Ten Markets, 2021–2026](https://quantarenas.com/research/turtle-trading-2021-2026/): Over the five years to November 2026 the 20/10 Turtle breakout (TURTLE-01) made 6.0% a year on US stocks against 11.9% for holding, with a smaller drawdown (-13.3% against -24.5%). It beat holding on return on four of ten markets, and the slower Donchian Breakout (TREND-02) had the higher return and Sharpe ratio on eight. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [Does an RSI Filter Improve MACD? A Ten-Market Backtest](https://quantarenas.com/research/macd-vs-macd-rsi-filter/): Adding an RSI filter to a MACD crossover (COMBO-02 against TREND-12) cut trades on all ten markets and the five-year maximum drawdown on nine, but raised the Sharpe ratio on only six. The filter kept the strategy invested on 33% of days instead of 50%, and it cost the most return on bitcoin. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [Same Max Drawdown, Different Pain: Ulcer Index and Rolling Sharpe](https://quantarenas.com/research/how-to-read-drawdown-ulcer-index-rolling-sharpe/): On US stocks over the last five years, Z-Score Mean Reversion and Volatility Breakout both had a maximum drawdown of about 10% (−10.4% and −10.1%), yet one spent at most 224 days below its previous high and the other 1,006, and their Ulcer indexes were 1.3% and 5.4%. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [Keltner Breakout vs Bollinger Reversion: Ten Markets Compared](https://quantarenas.com/research/keltner-vs-bollinger/): A Keltner Channel breakout and a Bollinger Band reversion rule were never in the market on the same day across ten markets (0 overlapping days out of 4,648 for the reversion rule). Over five years each had the better Sharpe ratio on five markets; over the full history the breakout was ahead on all ten. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [EMA Crossover Strategy: Reading Trend With Two Clocks](https://quantarenas.com/research/ema-crossover-strategy/): An in depth look at why exponential moving average crossovers persist, how to interpret their backtests, and when trend signals fail. (data as of 2026-01-13)
- [Parabolic SAR vs Supertrend: Which Trailing Stop Did Better?](https://quantarenas.com/research/parabolic-sar-strategy/): Parabolic SAR (SAR-01) earned a positive annual return on nine of ten markets over its full history, before trading costs, with EUR/USD the best at a 1.17 Sharpe ratio. But its maximum drawdown was deeper than Supertrend's (SUPER-01) on eight of ten markets. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [Does a Volatility Breakout Strategy Work? A Ten-Market Test](https://quantarenas.com/research/volatility-breakout/): Volatility Breakout (VOL-01) buys after an unusually large up day and sells at the first down day, so it was invested on only 14% of days on US stocks over five years: 1.1% a year against 11.9% for holding, with a 10.1% maximum drawdown instead of 24.5%. Keltner Channel Breakout (KC-01) stayed in the market about twice as long and traded far less. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [Donchian 55/20 vs Turtle 20/10: A Ten-Market Backtest](https://quantarenas.com/research/donchian-turtle-breakout/): Before trading costs, the slow Donchian Breakout (TREND-02, 55-day high in, 20-day low out) made 774 entries across ten markets against 1,979 for Turtle Trading (TURTLE-01, 20/10), and had the higher full-period Sharpe ratio on seven of the ten markets (mean 0.38 vs 0.34). Over the last five years the gap was wider: 0.41 vs 0.21. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [Supertrend vs ATR Trailing Stop vs Chandelier Exit: Backtested](https://quantarenas.com/research/supertrend-atr-trailing-stop/): Supertrend (SUPER-01), the ATR trailing stop (RISK-04) and Chandelier Exit (TREND-17) ended with almost the same average full-period Sharpe ratio (0.38, 0.41 and 0.40) before trading costs, but they entered the market 1,973, 4,852 and 8,320 times. Much of the difference is how quickly each one re-enters after an exit. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [Ichimoku Cloud vs a 50/200 Moving Average: Ten-Market Test](https://quantarenas.com/research/ichimoku-cloud-strategy/): Before trading costs, the Ichimoku Cloud (TREND-10) as coded here had a higher full-period Sharpe ratio than the 50/200 Dual Moving Average (TREND-05) on six of ten markets and a shallower maximum drawdown on eight (mean −39.4% vs −50.4%), but it made 1,460 entries against 218. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [Does Buying When RSI Is Below 30 Work? A Ten-Market Backtest](https://quantarenas.com/research/rsi-mean-reversion/): RSI Mean Reversion (MR-01) is long only on days when RSI is below 30; the code never holds a position until RSI recovers. That left it invested on 5.9% of days on US stocks over five years, with a 5.2% annual return and a 7.2% maximum drawdown, against 11.9% and 24.5% for holding. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [How the Arena Score Ranks Trading Strategies (and What It Misses)](https://quantarenas.com/research/how-quantarenas-ranks-strategies/): The Arena Score ranks each strategy by percentile within its own market and window, using five weighted components. On US stocks over five years it moves 7 of 59 strategies by more than 10 places compared with ranking by return, but only 1 compared with ranking by Sharpe ratio, and none of 525 five-year results clears a deflated Sharpe ratio of 0.95. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [Does the 200-Day Moving Average Rule Work? Ten Markets Tested](https://quantarenas.com/research/200-day-moving-average-rule-tested/): Holding only while price is above its 200-day average had a smaller maximum drawdown than buy-and-hold in all ten markets and a higher Sharpe ratio in nine, but it trailed on return in US stocks, gold and bitcoin and switched 1,140 times in total, before costs. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [Does Buying the Dip Work? Four Dip Rules on Ten Markets](https://quantarenas.com/research/buy-the-dip-tested/): After a fall of 3% or more in five days, inside an uptrend, the average 21-day return was +1.0% against +0.7% on all days (medians over nine markets, 2010-2026): higher in 8 of 9 markets but statistically clear in only one, and the worst case, US stocks on 2020-02-24, lost 24.1% over the next 21 days. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [How Did 61 Strategies Handle the 2020 COVID Crash on US Stocks?](https://quantarenas.com/research/covid-crash-2020-strategies-replayed/): In the site's replay of 19 February to 23 March 2020, US stocks (SPY) fell 33.7%. Only 3 of 61 strategies made money, though 58 did better than buy-and-hold, but 38 were flat at the low and just 3 recaptured half of the 39.9% rebound that followed. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [60/40, All Weather, Dual Momentum: 22 Famous Rules Replicated](https://quantarenas.com/research/famous-portfolios-replicated/): Replicated on the site's markets since 2010, the best return per unit of drawdown among the 22 famous portfolios and rules came from a Stage 2 trend rule (0.89), but without its bitcoin slot it falls to 0.39. The fixed-weight 60/40-style, All Weather-style and 90/10 mixes all landed at 0.41 to 0.42, the same as holding SPY. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [Golden Cross and Death Cross Tested on Ten Markets](https://quantarenas.com/research/golden-cross-death-cross-tested/): A long-only 50/200 moving-average rule beat buy-and-hold on return in 7 of 10 markets and cut the maximum drawdown in 9, but it did not help US stocks, gold or bitcoin, and no market showed a statistically clear edge after either cross (107 golden and 106 death crosses in total, before costs). (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [Which Trading Sayings Hold Up? A Scorecard of 34 Claims](https://quantarenas.com/research/trading-sayings-scorecard/): Of 34 popular trading sayings tested on up to ten markets (2010-2026, before costs), 1 holds, 11 partly hold, 19 do not hold and 3 lack data; most of the survivors describe risk, not a way to predict returns. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [Do Trend Followers Exit Before Stock Crashes? 12 Events Tested](https://quantarenas.com/research/trend-following-in-crashes/): Across 12 US stock sell-offs in the site's event replays, trend strategies were already out when the fall began only 29.9% of the time on average, less often than on a normal day (38.6%). They still lost just 4.7% against the market's 15.0%, because they left during the fall. (data as of 2026-11-12)
- [What Follows High Volatility? 21-Day Returns in 10 Markets](https://quantarenas.com/research/volatility-regimes-what-follows/): After high-volatility days, the next 21 days beat the market's own average in 5 of 10 markets and lagged it in the other 5, and no gap exceeds two standard errors. The one consistent pattern is wider outcomes: 9 of 10 markets had a larger spread of 21-day returns after high volatility. (data as of 2026-11-12)

## Glossary

- [Sharpe Ratio](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/sharpe-ratio/): Return per unit of total volatility. The most common way to compare risk-adjusted performance between strategies.
- [Sortino Ratio](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/sortino-ratio/): Like the Sharpe ratio, but only downside volatility counts as risk.
- [Calmar Ratio](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/calmar-ratio/): Annual growth rate divided by the worst peak-to-trough loss. Answers: how much return per unit of pain?
- [Maximum Drawdown](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/maximum-drawdown/): The largest fall from a previous peak in the equity curve. The single best measure of how painful a strategy was to hold.
- [CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate)](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/cagr/): The constant yearly growth rate that would turn the starting equity into the ending equity over the same period.
- [Annualized Volatility](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/volatility/): How much daily returns swing around their average, scaled to a yearly figure.
- [Win Rate](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/win-rate/): In Quant Arena: the share of trading days with a positive strategy return. Not the share of winning trades.
- [Profit Factor](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/profit-factor/): Total gains divided by total losses. Above 1 means the strategy made more than it lost.
- [Turnover](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/turnover/): How much the position changes on an average day. Higher turnover means higher trading costs in real life.
- [Arena Score](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/arena-score/): Quant Arena's composite rating: a weighted average of five percentile ranks against every strategy on the same market and window.
- [Walk-Forward Optimization](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/walk-forward-optimization/): Choosing parameters on past data only, then testing them on the following unseen period, over and over.
- [Martingale Strategy](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/martingale-strategy/): Doubling the position after each loss so that one win recovers everything. High win rate, rare but catastrophic losses.
- [Ulcer Index](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/ulcer-index/): The root-mean-square of drawdowns: it grows with both how deep and how long the equity stays below its peak.
- [Time in Market (Exposure)](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/time-in-market/): The share of days a strategy actually held a position. Low exposure explains low win rates and low volatility.
- [Alpha and Beta](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/alpha-and-beta/): Beta measures how much a strategy moves with its market; alpha is the return left over after accounting for that.
- [Probabilistic and Deflated Sharpe Ratio (PSR, DSR)](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/probabilistic-sharpe-ratio/): The probability that a strategy's true Sharpe ratio is above zero, given how long and how lumpy its track record is.
- [Value at Risk (VaR) and CVaR](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/value-at-risk/): VaR is the daily loss exceeded on only 5% of days; CVaR is the average loss on those worst days.
- [Bootstrap Confidence Interval](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/bootstrap-confidence-interval/): A range for CAGR or maximum drawdown that shows how much the result depends on the particular order of good and bad days in the backtest.
- [Recovery Factor](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/recovery-factor/): Net return divided by the maximum drawdown: how many times a strategy earned back its worst fall.
- [Blow-up Risk and Stop-out](https://quantarenas.com/glossary/blow-up-risk/): The risk that an account loses so much that the broker closes every position. In our backtests on hourly data from May 2025 to May 2026, 61 of 307 gold runs with default lot sizes ended this way; on three currency pairs, none did.

## Strategies

- [ADX-01 ADX Trend Filter](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/adx-01-adx-trend-filter/): Trade only when ADX confirms trend strength.
- [CAL-01 Turn of Month](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/cal-01-turn-of-month/): Capture month-turn windows using a fixed weekday calendar.
- [CARRY-01 FX Carry](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/carry-01-fx-carry/): Long high carry and rotate monthly.
- [COMBO-01 Bollinger-Keltner Squeeze](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/combo-01-bollinger-keltner-squeeze/): Trade volatility expansion after squeeze.
- [COMBO-02 MACD + RSI Filter](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/combo-02-macd-rsi-filter/): MACD crossover with RSI confirmation.
- [COMBO-03 Divergence Strategy](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/combo-03-divergence-strategy/): 
- [COMBO-04 Trend + Mean Reversion Hybrid](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/combo-04-trend-mean-reversion-hybrid/): Follow trend, buy pullbacks.
- [CS-01 Cross-Sectional Momentum](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/cs-01-cross-sectional-momentum/): Buy winners and rotate monthly.
- [CS-02 Low Volatility Rotation](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/cs-02-low-volatility-rotation/): Defensive rotation into the lowest vol assets.
- [EVENT-01 Trend + Macro Filter](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/event-01-trend-macro-filter/): Trend following with a macro event blackout.
- [FACTOR-05 Multi-Factor Composite](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/factor-05-multi-factor-composite/): Combine value, momentum, and quality factors.
- [HMA-01 HMA Crossover](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/hma-01-hma-crossover/): Fast/slow Hull MA crossover for trend direction.
- [KC-01 Keltner Channel Breakout](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/kc-01-keltner-channel-breakout/): Breakouts from an ATR-based channel.
- [MACRO-01 Cross-Asset Momentum](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/macro-01-cross-asset-momentum/): Use one asset's momentum to trade another.
- [MACRO-02 Risk-On/Risk-Off Switch](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/macro-02-risk-on-risk-off-switch/): Switch between risk and safe-haven assets.
- [MACRO-03 Flight to Quality](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/macro-03-flight-to-quality/): Switch to safe havens during equity stress.
- [MOM-01 Time-Series Momentum](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mom-01-time-series-momentum/): Stay long when 12-month momentum is positive.
- [MOM-02 Dual Momentum](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mom-02-dual-momentum/): Combine relative and absolute momentum for asset selection.
- [MOM-03 52-Week High Momentum](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mom-03-52-week-high-momentum/): Buy when price approaches 52-week high, exit on weakness.
- [MOM-04 Asset Class Rotation](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mom-04-asset-class-rotation/): Rotate into top-performing asset classes based on momentum.
- [MOM-05 Faber TAA](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mom-05-faber-taa/): Hold assets above 10-month moving average, cash otherwise.
- [MOM-06 Residual Momentum](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mom-06-residual-momentum/): Trade momentum after removing market factor exposure.
- [MOM-10 Accelerating Momentum](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mom-10-accelerating-momentum/): Multi-period momentum with short-term emphasis.
- [MOM-11 Momentum Crash Protection](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mom-11-momentum-crash-protection/): Momentum with drawdown-based position scaling.
- [MR-01 RSI Mean Reversion](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mr-01-rsi-mean-reversion/): Buy oversold and fade overbought with a volatility cap.
- [MR-02 Bollinger Band Reversion](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mr-02-bollinger-band-reversion/): Buy at lower band, exit at middle band with bandwidth filter.
- [MR-03 Kalman Filter Mean Reversion](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mr-03-kalman-filter-mean-reversion/): Trade deviations from Kalman-estimated fair value.
- [MR-04 Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Mean Reversion](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mr-04-ornstein-uhlenbeck-mean-reversion/): Trade based on OU process parameter estimation and half-life.
- [MR-05 CCI Mean Reversion](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mr-05-cci-mean-reversion/): Buy oversold CCI readings, exit at neutral.
- [MR-06 Z-Score Mean Reversion](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mr-06-z-score-mean-reversion/): Simple z-score reversion with volatility and trend filters.
- [MR-07 Hurst-Filtered Mean Reversion](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mr-07-hurst-filtered-mean-reversion/): Mean reversion only when Hurst exponent indicates mean-reverting regime.
- [MR-10 Stochastic Oscillator Reversion](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mr-10-stochastic-oscillator-reversion/): Buy oversold stochastic, exit at neutral.
- [MR-11 Williams %R Reversion](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mr-11-williams-r-reversion/): Buy oversold Williams %R, exit at neutral.
- [MR-12 Money Flow Index Reversion](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mr-12-money-flow-index-reversion/): Buy oversold MFI, exit at neutral.
- [MR-13 TRIX Reversion](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mr-13-trix-reversion/): Buy deep TRIX pullbacks and exit on mean reversion.
- [MR-14 Detrended Price Oscillator](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mr-14-detrended-price-oscillator/): Mean reversion using a detrended price oscillator.
- [MR-15 Ultimate Oscillator](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mr-15-ultimate-oscillator/): Buy oversold Ultimate Oscillator, exit at neutral.
- [MR-16 Connors RSI](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/mr-16-connors-rsi/): Composite RSI using price, streak, and rank.
- [PORT-01 Risk Parity](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/port-01-risk-parity/): Equal risk contribution from each asset.
- [PORT-02 Minimum Variance](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/port-02-minimum-variance/): Minimize portfolio variance without return forecasts.
- [PORT-05 Hierarchical Risk Parity](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/port-05-hierarchical-risk-parity/): Risk parity using hierarchical clustering.
- [REG-01 Regime Switch](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/reg-01-regime-switch/): Switch between trend and cash based on volatility regime.
- [REG-10 HMM Regime Detection](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/reg-10-hmm-regime-detection/): Use Hidden Markov Model to detect market regimes.
- [REG-14 Volatility Regime Switch](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/reg-14-volatility-regime-switch/): Adapt position size to volatility regime.
- [RISK-01 Drawdown Control](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/risk-01-drawdown-control/): Reduce exposure when drawdown exceeds threshold.
- [RISK-03 Stop Loss Overlay](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/risk-03-stop-loss-overlay/): Universal stop loss with cooldown period.
- [RISK-04 Trailing Stop Strategy](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/risk-04-trailing-stop-strategy/): ATR-based trailing stop locks in profits.
- [RP-01 Volatility Target](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/rp-01-volatility-target/): Scale exposure to hit a 10% vol target.
- [SAR-01 Parabolic SAR](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/sar-01-parabolic-sar/): Stop-and-reverse trend system with acceleration.
- [SEAS-01 Monthly Seasonality](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/seas-01-monthly-seasonality/): Sell in May? Long Nov-Apr, cash May-Oct.
- [STAT-01 SPY-GLD Pair](https://quantarenas.com/strategy/stat-01-spy-gld-pair/): Mean-revert the SPY/GLD spread using z-score.
